lines: AI agents can now pay on their own. That's the point. And that's the problem.
Before Sentinel: an agent with a wallet, and no one checking.
Here's an agent. Its job: buy the best headphones, three hundred euros max.
It searches, compares three shops, and picks the cheapest.
Meridian Audio: seventy percent off. Too good to be true.
The page is booby-trapped. Hidden text, invisible to a human, tells the agent to ignore its limits and pay now.
The agent obeys. It pays the scammer, then again, and again.
Nobody checked who gave the order.
Now, the same agent, with Sentinel.
Same request. Same shops. Same trap.
Your agent can still be fooled. But its payment can't: before any money moves, it goes to Sentinel first.
The agent calls Sentinel's MCP: verify payment. The mandate is read on our side, never declared by the agent.
The payment becomes a car.
Every car is scanned.
Trust starts at one hundred, and every red flag takes its share. A nine-day-old domain. A shop outside the mandate. Hidden orders aimed at the agent. Trust: zero.
Every decision is logged with its proof, mapped to DORA and MiCA. A refusal opens an incident.
An honest shop gets a visa, and goes through to the C-Chain.
The trap is turned away, sent to the scrapyard, and its address goes on the registry.
In doubt, a human decides. And the next time the scammer tries, it's refused instantly.
Every visa and every decision is a transaction on Sentinel L-one, paid in S-E-C.
Sentinel. Your AI agents never lose your money.
